lessons.title: Being a good friend: kind words and kind actions
objectives: Describe what makes a good friend
Use kind words and avoid unkind nicknames
Link kindness to our Tarbiyyah Compass values

keywords.def: someone you trust, enjoy and care for
being gentle, helpful and caring
a name used instead of someone's real name
good manners and behaviour
to make sure everyone can join in

starter: Name one way to be kind in a live lesson.
Who is a trusted adult you can go to?

teach.heading: What makes a good friend?
teach.note: Say bismillah. Recap the Tarbiyyah Compass values from earlier years (Resilience, Eeman, Contentment, Integrity, Progress, Excellence). Today links to Integrity and Excellence in how we treat others. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Anonymous questions can go to the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day. Ask: ‘What do you like about your best friend?’ Take answers without names if pupils prefer.

teach.heading: Kind words
bullets: Say please, thank you and sorry
teach.note: Cite plainly: the Prophet (peace be upon him) taught that a smile is charity (Tirmidhi). Model giving a sincere compliment to a pupil's work. Ask: ‘How do you feel when someone is kind to you?’ Misconception: kindness is only for friends. It is for everyone.

teach.heading: Names we use
bullets: Qur'an 49:11: do not call each other bad names
teach.note: Cite plainly: Qur'an 49:11 tells believers not to mock one another or call each other offensive nicknames. Distinguish a kind family nickname that the person loves from a name that makes someone feel small. Ask: ‘How can we check?’ (ask them; stop if they dislike it).

teach.heading: Including everyone
bullets: Be a friend to new classmates
teach.note: Role-play: someone new joins the group in a break-out room or class game. Ask: ‘What can you say?’ Model: ‘Would you like to join us?’ Link to the hadith that none of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself (Bukhari and Muslim). Keep language simple for Year 3.

practice: Sort into kind or unkind: (a) ‘You can’t play.’ (b) ‘Would you like to join?’ (c) Laughing at someone’s mistake. (d) Sharing your pencil.
What could you say to a new child in class?
Rewrite this to be kinder: ‘Move, slowcoach!’
independent: Write a ‘kind friend’ poster with five qualities and one example of a kind sentence, decorated with pattern.
Role-play with a partner: inviting someone to join a game, using polite words.
Write three kind compliments you could say to classmates.
exit: Name two ways to be a good friend.
Why should we avoid unkind nicknames?
lessons.homework: Do one kind act for someone at home and write one sentence about how it made them feel.
lessons.send: SEND: use picture cards for kind and unkind actions. EAL: key phrases in simple English with visuals. Stretch: write a short story where a child includes a lonely friend.

lessons.title: When friends fall out: solving problems and spotting bullying
objectives: Use steps to solve a disagreement kindly
Explain the difference between falling out and bullying
Know who to tell if bullying happens

keywords.def: when people do not agree
to say sorry and mean it
hurting someone on purpose, again and again
someone who helps when they see unkindness
a grown-up who helps keep you safe

starter: Give one kind word you can say to a friend.
Why should we use real names?

teach.heading: Disagreements happen
bullets: It is normal to feel cross
Anger is a feeling, not a rule
teach.note: Say bismillah. Normalise disagreements: all friends have them. Cite plainly: the Prophet (peace be upon him) said the strong person is the one who controls himself when angry (Bukhari and Muslim). Ask: ‘What does your body feel like when you are cross?’ Take answers: hot face, fast heart. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Anonymous questions can go to the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Steps to sort it out
bullets: Say how you feel: ‘I felt sad when…’
Find a fair answer and say sorry
teach.note: Model the steps with a scenario: two friends both want the same football turn. Show how to use ‘I’ statements rather than blame. Ask pupils to rehearse: ‘I felt left out when you ran off.’ Misconception: saying sorry fixes everything. We also need to change what we do.

teach.heading: Falling out or bullying?
bullets: Falling out: once, equal, both upset
Bullying can be words, hitting, leaving out, or online
Bullying is never the victim's fault
teach.note: Draw a two-column table on the board. Ask pupils to place examples. Emphasise that bullying involves power: one person or group keeps hurting another who finds it hard to stop it. Check understanding with thumbs up or down. Keep examples invented, not real pupils.

teach.heading: What can we do?
bullets: Walk away and tell a trusted adult
Help the person who is hurt
teach.note: Teach being an upstander: kindly support the targeted child and tell an adult. Reassure pupils that telling is not ‘snitching’, it is keeping people safe. Name trusted adults at home and in school. If a pupil discloses bullying, record and pass to the DSL or class teacher according to the Anti-Bullying and Safeguarding policies.

practice: Is it falling out or bullying? (a) Two friends argue once about a game. (b) A child is left out every break time on purpose. (c) A child keeps sending unkind messages in a game chat.
Put the steps in order: say sorry / stop and breathe / listen / say how you feel.
Who are three trusted adults you could tell?
independent: Write or act out a short conversation where two friends solve a disagreement using the steps.
Make a ‘What to do if I see bullying’ card with three actions.
Write one ‘I felt… when…’ sentence for an invented problem.
exit: What is the difference between falling out and bullying?
Name one thing you can do if you are being bullied.
lessons.homework: Tell a trusted adult at home one of the steps for solving a problem kindly and ask them to share a time they solved a disagreement.
lessons.send: SEND: provide visual steps cards. EAL: key phrases ‘Stop’, ‘Tell’, ‘Sorry’ with pictures. Stretch: write advice for a younger child about handling a falling out.

lessons.title: Keeping safe at home and online; trusted adults
lessons.bigQuestion: A pop-up says 'Click here for free game coins!'. What would you do?
objectives: To understand how to keep safe at home and online and who our trusted adults are
successCriteria: Most: spot dangers at home and online and say what to do
Some: explain the online rules for our Teams lessons and why they keep us safe

keywords.def: a grown-up who keeps you safe and listens
something that could hurt you
kept to yourself, not shared
using the internet

hook.text: A pop-up says 'Click here for free game coins!'. What would you do?
hook.a: Do not click; tell a trusted adult.

islamicLink.text: Islam asks us to protect ourselves from harm. Allah says: 'Do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction' (al-Baqarah 2:195). Asking a trusted adult for help is a wise and brave choice.

starter.q: What helps hearts find rest? A) remembering Allah B) shouting C) staying up late
Name a calm-down strategy.
How do germs spread?
Who is someone who looks after you?

teach.heading: Safe at home
teach.note: Sort.

teach.heading: Safe online
bullets: Only use school accounts for lessons
teach.note: Teams rules: first name, camera on in a shared room, chat only for learning, never share a password or address.

teach.heading: Trusted adults
teach.note: If one adult does not listen, tell another.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: Someone you do not know messages you in a game. What do you do?
options: Do not reply and tell a trusted adult
check.why: Strangers online may not be who they say; a trusted adult helps you stay safe.

practice.q: Is it safe to tell a game player your school's name?
practice.model: Teacher asks: could it help a stranger find me? Yes, so keep it private.

practice.a: For example: my mum and my teacher.

independent.q: Core: Draw a 'helping hand' outline of your own hand and write a trusted adult on each finger (pupil PDF).
independent.model: Teacher writes 'Mum' and 'my teacher' on two fingers.

independent.q: Extend: Write three online safety rules for our Teams lessons.
independent.a: For example: first name only; chat for learning; never share a password.

independent.q: Stretch: Explain what you would do if something online made you feel worried, and why.
independent.a: Stop, do not reply, tell a trusted adult, because they can help keep me safe.

exit.q: A pop-up offers free coins. You should... A) click it B) not click and tell an adult C) give your password
exit.a: B) not click and tell an adult
options: Not click and tell an adult

exit.q: Big question: who are your trusted adults?
exit.a: For example: parents, grandparents and my teacher.

lessons.homework: Show your helping hand to your family and put it near where you use your device.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards for home dangers. EAL: safe, danger, private, trusted. Stretch: what to do if a trusted adult is busy.

lessons.title: Exercise, rest and sleep at home
lessons.bigQuestion: We learn on screens at our online school. How can we make sure our bodies still move enough?
objectives: To understand why our bodies need exercise, rest and sleep, and how to fit them into a day at home
successCriteria: All: name three ways to be active at home
Most: say how much sleep children need and why
Some: plan a healthy daily routine with activity, learning and sleep

keywords.def: moving our body to make it stronger
a break to let the body recover
the things we do at the same times each day
time spent looking at a screen

hook.text: We learn on screens at our online school. How can we make sure our bodies still move enough?
hook.a: Plan active breaks: stretch between lessons, play outside, help at home.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said that two blessings many people waste are good health and free time (al-Bukhari). Moving our bodies, resting well and sleeping after Isha help us use both well.

starter.q: Biggest part of a balanced plate?
What does tayyib mean?
Name a protein food.
What is the best drink?

teach.heading: Why exercise?
bullets: About an hour of activity a day
teach.note: UK guidance for children: an average of at least 60 minutes of activity a day.

teach.heading: Active at home
teach.note: Quick 1-minute stretch together now (no music).

teach.heading: Sleep
bullets: Sleep early after Isha, wake for Fajr
teach.note: A regular bedtime helps the body clock.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: About how much sleep do children your age need?
check.why: Children aged 6 to 12 need about 9 to 12 hours.

practice.q: Show me: name three ways to be active indoors.
practice.a: For example: star jumps, skipping, stretching, tidying.
practice.model: Teacher lists three and does a star jump.

practice.q: Why should screens go off before bed?
practice.a: Screens keep the brain awake and make it harder to sleep.

independent.q: Core: Fill in your own daily routine sheet with lessons, activity, meals, prayer times and bedtime (pupil PDF).
independent.a: A routine with at least 60 minutes of activity and 9 or more hours of sleep.

independent.q: Extend: Add three 2-minute stretch breaks between lessons to your routine.
Stretch: Explain how sleep helps your learning.
independent.a: The brain rests and stores what we learned; we concentrate better.

exit.q: How much activity should children get each day? A) 10 minutes B) about 60 minutes C) none
Big question: how will you move enough on online school days?
exit.a: For example: stretch breaks and play outside after lessons.

lessons.homework: Follow your routine for three days and tick each activity and bedtime.
lessons.send: SEND: routine sheet with pictures. EAL: wake, sleep, exercise. Stretch: count your active minutes for a day.

lessons.title: Healthy eating: a balanced plate
lessons.bigQuestion: Could you be healthy eating only chips, even if they were halal?
objectives: To understand how a balanced plate gives our bodies what they need
successCriteria: All: name the main food groups
Most: build a balanced plate with the right amounts
Some: explain why we eat sugary and fatty foods only a little
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: thanking Allah for food, saying Bismillah and Alhamdulillah

keywords.def: the right amount of each kind of food
foods that do a similar job, like fruit and vegetables
allowed in Islam (حَلَال)
good and wholesome (طَيِّب)

hook.text: Could you be healthy eating only chips, even if they were halal?
hook.a: No: food should be halal and tayyib (good), and balanced.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'O mankind, eat from whatever is on earth that is lawful and good' (al-Baqarah 2:168). Muslims choose food that is halal and also tayyib: good for the body.

starter.q: How long should we wash our hands? A) 2 seconds B) 20 seconds C) 2 minutes
What is a need?
starter.a: Something we must have to live.

starter.q: What do we say before eating?
Name a fruit.

teach.heading: The food groups
bullets: Protein: beans, eggs, fish, halal meat
teach.note: Use the Eatwell Guide picture.

teach.heading: A balanced plate
teach.note: Rough shares of the Eatwell Guide (about a third fruit and veg, a third starchy foods).

teach.heading: Sugary and fatty foods
bullets: Too much harms teeth and heart
teach.note: Sweets and fizzy drinks are not on the main plate.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: Which should be the biggest part of our plate?
check.why: Fruit and vegetables are the largest part of a balanced plate.

practice.q: Which food group is rice in?
practice.model: Teacher asks: does it fill us with energy like bread and potatoes? Yes, so starchy foods.

practice.a: For example: beans, eggs, lentils, fish, halal chicken.

practice.q: Is a fizzy drink an every-day drink?
practice.a: No: water is best; fizzy drinks only sometimes.

independent.q: Core: Draw a balanced plate for your dinner with the right amounts of each group (pupil PDF).
independent.a: Half fruit and veg, starchy food, some protein, a little dairy.
independent.model: Teacher draws a plate with rice, lentil dal and salad and labels each group.

independent.q: Extend: Write a menu for one healthy day: breakfast, lunch, dinner, a snack.
independent.a: A balanced day with fruit and vegetables at most meals.

independent.q: Stretch: Explain why a plate of only chips is not tayyib for our body.
independent.a: It has too much fat and starch and no fruit, vegetables or protein.

exit.q: Halal and tayyib means food that is... A) allowed and good B) only tasty C) only sweet
Big question: could you be healthy eating only chips? Why?
exit.a: No: our body needs a balance of food groups.

lessons.homework: Help prepare one balanced meal at home and draw your plate.
lessons.send: SEND: food picture cards to place on a plate. EAL: food group names with pictures. Stretch: compare two lunchboxes.

lessons.title: Staying healthy: hand washing, teeth and germs
lessons.bigQuestion: You sneeze into your hand and then open the fridge. Where are the germs now?
objectives: To understand how germs spread and how hygiene stops them
successCriteria: All: show the steps of good handwashing
Most: explain two ways germs spread
Some: explain how wudu and good habits help keep us clean
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: taharah as part of worship

keywords.def: a tiny living thing that can cause illness
pass from one place or person to another
keeping clean to stay healthy
a sticky layer of germs on teeth

hook.text: You sneeze into your hand and then open the fridge. Where are the germs now?
hook.a: On your hand and on the fridge handle, ready for the next person.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said that cleanliness (purity) is half of faith (Muslim). Muslims wash for wudu before prayer, use the miswak, and wash hands before and after eating.

starter.q: How many hours of sleep do children need? A) 4 B) about 10 C) 16
Name one way to be active at home.
When should screens go off?
What is a balanced plate?
starter.a: The right amount of each food group.

teach.heading: How germs spread
teach.note: Pepper experiment (at home with a grown-up): pepper on water, touch with a soapy finger, the pepper rushes away.

teach.heading: Stopping germs
bullets: Catch it, bin it, kill it
Wash hands with soap for 20 seconds
teach.note: Catch a sneeze in a tissue, bin it, wash hands.

teach.heading: Teeth
bullets: Brush twice a day for 2 minutes
teach.note: Plaque germs make acid that harms teeth.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: You need to sneeze. Best thing to do?
options: Catch it in a tissue, bin it, wash hands
check.why: Catch it, bin it, kill it stops germs reaching hands and surfaces.

practice.q: Put in order: rinse, wet, soap, dry, rub for 20 seconds.
practice.a: Wet, soap, rub for 20 seconds, rinse, dry.
For example: sneezes and dirty hands.

independent.q: Core: Make a 'Stop the germs' poster with four rules (words and pictures of objects, no people).
independent.a: Four rules: wash hands, catch sneezes, brush teeth, do not share cups.
independent.model: Teacher writes rule 1 with a soap picture.

independent.q: Extend: With a grown-up, try the pepper and soap experiment and write what happened.
independent.a: The pepper moved away from the soap.

independent.q: Stretch: Explain how wudu helps keep us clean.
independent.a: We wash our hands, mouth, nose, face, arms and feet several times a day.

exit.q: Plaque is... A) a toothbrush B) a sticky layer of germs on teeth C) a type of food
exit.a: B) a sticky layer of germs on teeth
options: A sticky layer of germs on teeth

exit.q: Big question: after a sneeze into your hand and touching the fridge, where are the germs?
exit.a: On your hand and the fridge handle.

lessons.homework: Teach someone at home 'Catch it, bin it, kill it'.
lessons.send: SEND: step cards with pictures. EAL: germ, spread, sneeze. Stretch: find out why soap works better than water alone.

lessons.title: Feeling happy: what helps us feel good
lessons.bigQuestion: What is one small thing that made you smile this week?
objectives: To understand which things help us feel happy and calm, and what to do when we feel sad
successCriteria: All: name three things that make you feel happy
Most: describe a way to calm down when upset
Some: explain how helping others and remembering Allah can make us feel good

keywords.def: how we feel inside, like happy, sad or worried
peaceful and relaxed
being thankful (shukr, شُكْر)
doing good for others

hook.text: What is one small thing that made you smile this week?

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest' (ar-Ra'd 13:28). Saying Alhamdulillah for our blessings and helping others are ways to feel content.

starter.q: What should you do when you sneeze?
starter.a: Catch it in a tissue, bin it, wash hands.
options: Catch it, bin it, kill it

starter.q: How long should we brush our teeth?
Name a feeling.
starter.a: For example: happy, sad, angry, worried.

starter.q: What do we say when something good happens?

teach.heading: All feelings are normal
bullets: We can choose what we do
teach.note: Feelings are not good or bad; actions can be.

teach.heading: Things that help us feel good
teach.note: Ask for examples.

teach.heading: When we feel upset
teach.note: Practise slow breathing: in for 4, out for 4.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: You feel cross. What is a good first step?
check.why: Breathing slowly calms the body so we can choose what to do next.

practice.q: Show me three things that make you happy.
practice.a: Any three (for example: playing with my brother, reading, helping cook).
practice.model: Teacher shares three of their own: a walk, reading Qur'an, cooking with family.

practice.q: Show me the breathing: in for 4, out for 4.

independent.q: Core: Make a 'happy jar' sheet: write or draw five things you are grateful for (pupil PDF).
Extend: Write one kind thing you will do for someone this week.
independent.a: For example: help set the table.

independent.q: Stretch: Explain why helping others can make us feel good too.
independent.a: It brings us closer to others and to Allah, and we feel useful.

exit.q: Shukr means... A) thankfulness B) anger C) sleep
Big question: name one thing that helps you feel good.
exit.a: For example: helping someone, saying Alhamdulillah.

lessons.homework: Each night this week, tell your family one thing you are grateful for.
lessons.send: SEND: feelings cards with symbols (no faces: weather symbols for feelings). EAL: happy, sad, calm. Stretch: write a short du'a of thanks.
